name: Marina Caprotti
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2024)
forbes_bio: Marina Caprotti inherited most of her wealth from her late father, Bernardo Caprotti, who was the founder of Italian supermarket chain Esselunga.
Bernardo left his second wife Giuliana and daughter Marina a 67% stake in the company, and gave the remaining third to his other two children.
In 2020, Giuliana and Marina bought out the remaining stake for nearly 2 billion Euros.
Marina was named executive chair of Esselunga in 2020.

name: Tatiana Volodina
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Tatiana Volodina's fortune is derived from L'Etoile, a well-known perfume and cosmetics retail chain with 1,000 locations in 250 cities across Russia.
Volodina owns L'Etoile through Alkor, a holding company in which she has a controlling stake.
Alkor also owns Podruzhka, a smaller cosmetics chain.
L'Etoile and Podruzhka ( also know as "Girlfriend") saw combined sales of over $1 billion.
After earning a degree in economic cybernetics, Volodina worked for Shiseido and Estée Lauder Companies and helped build their businesses in Russia.

name: Lu Yiwen

forbes_bio: Lu Yiwen is a cofounder of jewelry supplier DR Corp.
DR went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2021.
The company is headquartered in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen.

name: Lee Su-jin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Lee Su-jin is the founder and CEO of South Korean travel superapp Yanolja.
SoftBank's Vision Fund 2 invested $1.7 billion in the company in 2021.
Orphaned as a child, Lee worked as a janitor at love hotels before starting Yanolja in 2005.
forbes_facts: Yanolja means "Hey, let's play" in Korean.

name: Su Qingcan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026); Hurun China (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Su Qingnan chairs Huaxia Eye Hospital, a provider of healthcare services headquartered in China's southeastern city of Xiamen.
Huaxia also serves patients in Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal and Sri Lanka.
Su emerged as a billionaire after Huaxia went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in November 2022.

name: Robyn Jones
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023-2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Robyn and Mark Jones are the cofounders of Goosehead Insurance, where Mark is chairman and CEO, and Robyn is vice chairman.
The Alberta natives were teenage sweethearts and married each other straight out of high school.
Robyn raised their six children while Mark, who was once a truck driver, went to college, attended Harvard Business School and consulted at Bain.
Frustrated with her husband's lifestyle, Robyn started a property and casualty insurance agency in 2003. Mark left Bain in 2004 to join the business.
The couple took Goosehead public in 2018 and as a family own more than 50% of the $117 million (2020 sales) business with nearly 1,500 franchises.
forbes_facts: Goosehead is named after her granddaughter, Lucy "Goosehead."

name: Mike Danson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
forbes_bio: Mike Danson is the CEO of GlobalData, which provides data analytics to such customers as Schweppes and Saab.
The son of two teachers, neither of whom went to university, Danson went to Oxford University and got his start in consulting.
Danson founded an earlier company, Datamonitor Financial, in his London flat in 1990, reportedly funding it with credit cards.
He took it public and reportedly pocketed more than $200 million when it was acquired in 2007. GlobalData later bought back parts of that first business.
The grandson of Wigan miners, he now owns his hometown's soccer team, Wigan Athletic FC. and rugby team Wigan Warriors as well as left-leaning publication New Statesman.
forbes_facts: His Danson Foundation offers up to 60 paid internships in London each year to undergrads of Oxford's St Anne's College, where he graduated in 1982 with a law degree.

name: Koo Bon-joon
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2011-2021); Hurun Global (2014-2024)
forbes_bio: Koo Bon-joon is the chairman of LX Group, whose main subsidiary LG International holds interests in energy, tech, tourism and industrial materials.
Koo is the second oldest of the Koo brothers of the LG Group, Korea's No. 4 conglomerate.
The bulk of his fortune is derived from the family's de facto holding company LG Corp.
He led the LG International joint venture with Philips, which became LG Display in 2008 and eventually the world's leading LCD manufacturer.
forbes_facts: He started his career with AT&T.
He is largely credited with turning around what was once LG's money-losing cellphone business.

name: Zhou Wen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023-2026); Forbes annual (2021-2023); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun China (2010-2026)
forbes_bio: Zhou Wen chairs Shanghai Pret Composites, a supplier of plastics and composites.
He worked as an engineer at SAIC Volkswagen Automotive, a Volkswagen joint venture, in China early in his career.
Shanghai Pret Composites listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2009.
Zhou holds an executive MBA degree from Fudan University.
In 2025 his son Zhenlun Zhou was appointed to vice chairman and vice general manager of the company.
